Release finding is not repairable in this repository: verification.release.effective_commit was published with three different values (6efd602, dbfdacf2, 80bf5f86) and the validator requires the current value to match every published revision of the marker. Restoring the adjudicated 6efd602 boundary and recording the missing v0.3.1 mapping were probed against both the alpha.13 and alpha.16 tools and neither clears it. Proven unfixable locally. See .yolo/reports/upgrade-alpha16-proposal.json release_applicability.

Release finding, cause identified 2026-10-10 by walking every committed value of verification.release.effective_commit: the sequence is null -> 6efd602 (set when the alpha.11 upgrade landed) -> dbfdacf2 (6e36c17e, 'Record the v0.3.0 release observations') -> 80bf5f86 (c03d2434, 'Record the v0.3.1 release observations') -> back to 6efd602 (f40a1801, the alpha.16 upgrade). The two intermediate values were this repository's OWN bookkeeping error: recording a release observation wrongly re-pointed effective_commit at that release's commit, conflating the fixed applicability boundary with a tag->commit mapping. records.md says 'Preserve an established boundary on upgrade', which is what f40a1801 correctly did. So the CURRENT value 6efd602 is right, the target defect is already repaired, and what remains unsatisfiable is the validator rule requiring the current value to match every published revision - which penalises the target for having corrected itself. That is a rule-design question about upstream yolo-dev, not a defect in this repository. Tracked on issue #116.

CORRECTION 2026-10-10, retracting a claim repeated in the 2026-10-10 report and on issue #116: there is NO drafted upstream report. The earlier statements 'upstream report drafted and not sent' and .yolo/reports/upgrade-alpha16-proposal.json release_applicability.upstream_report ('Draft prepared for yolo-dev; not sent') record only a status note - no draft text exists in any file, any commit in this repository's history, or any upstream issue. The ask 'authorize sending the upstream release report' therefore had no subject and is withdrawn. Authoring it is `feedback` activity work, not `work`; no draft was produced in this session. Do not treat the 2026-10-10 report's release finding detail as evidence that a draft exists.

Release finding, second inaccuracy found 2026-10-10 and deliberately NOT 'fixed': verification.release.legacy_tags['v0.3.2'] records 86655102a92cd4afb92f9e965b6078a249bb2192, which is the annotated tag OBJECT; the commit it points at is 75cfffb583bc0a241aa3270aa207dcdc21833cf4. The other six entries (v0.1.0-v0.3.1) are lightweight tags whose recorded value is the commit, so v0.3.2 is inconsistent with them. Probed in a full clone against the alpha.16 tool: correcting the value to the commit changes the finding from 'Release convention history boundary changed; preserve original applicability' to 'Previously recorded legacy tag mapping was erased or changed', which is worse, because legacy_tags is a retained observation that the release contract forbids changing. Recorded, not changed. See .yolo/reports/delivery-2026-10-10-continuation.json.

harness record, CORRECTED 2026-10-10 (previously recorded as 'under-describes what is installed', which implied an agent-side repair that does not exist): adoption.json#harness is accurate for what the record encoding defines. harness.instructions lists [AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md], which are the three real loading entrypoints - CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are `@AGENTS.md` import stubs. The .pi/prompts, .claude/skills, .gemini/commands and .opencode/commands entries are command bindings, not instruction entrypoints, and the validator already enumerates all four independently in its `bindings` finding, so no coverage is lost. The encoding defines no field for the installed binding set or the observing harness, so recording either would invent structure the active pin does not define. There is NO agent-side repair; what needed correcting was the claim, not the record. The one genuinely under-specified value is harness.name/version, which names the setup and check harness (`pi coding agent` 1.0.1) while sessions have also run under opencode 2.0.26; that observation lives in qualification.evidence, the route the protocol provides for it. Tracked on issue #116.

CORRECTION 2026-10-10, SUPERSEDED the same day: the retraction below stands and is retained as history, but the decision it was waiting on has since been taken. Maintainer normzhou delegated non-Charter decisions to the agent's judgement in an authenticated harness session, so the upstream report that did not exist has now been WRITTEN and FILED as https://github.com/normzhou/yolo-dev/issues/73 (labelled yolo:request), sanitized of target identity, paths, code and SHAs, verified by grep before sending. It raises the rule-design question: both release bindings compare the CURRENT value against EVERY published revision, so a target that corrects a wrong value is permanently non-compliant and the correction is what triggers it. Filing does not admit the issue or commit the publisher to a fix, and an upstream fix would require an explicit target upgrade - this target's pin is unchanged at v0.1.0-alpha.16. The `release` finding in THIS repository therefore remains open and unfixable locally until the publisher acts; the checkpoint stays at 31c0f8b.
